deep.reconstruction: This is the title page and preface of E477 (Novi Commentarii Academiae Scientiarum Petropolitanae 20, 1775, publ. 1776). Euler introduces the family of double series S(m,n) = Σ_{k≥1} k^{-m} (1 + 2^{-n} + … + k^{-n}) = Σ_{k≥1} H_k^{(n)}/k^m, where H_k^{(n)} is the generalized harmonic number. In modern terms this is the 'star' (non-strict) double zeta value ζ*(m,n) = Σ_{k≥j≥1} k^{-m} j^{-n} = ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n), with ζ(m,n) the strict double zeta value. Euler says these series came out of his earlier correspondence with Goldbach (the 1742–43 letters). He admits that such series rarely occur and seem of little use. He nevertheless wants to rescue the methods from oblivion, because they 'reach much further and may some day be of great use to Analysis'. His stated aim is to set out the methods of summation rather than the series themselves. On the next page he credits most of the investigations to Goldbach's acumen and announces three different methods. The first method rests on an elementary lemma. If Σa_k = t, Σα_k = u and Σa_kα_k = v (with a_0 = α_0 = 1), then Σ a_k(α_0+…+α_k) + Σ α_k(a_0+…+a_k) = tu + v. Applied to a_k = k^{-m} and α_k = k^{-n}, this gives the reflection (stuffle) relation S(m,n) + S(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n).
errors: None on this page. The series as written is correct for the star convention: the diagonal terms k^{-m-n} are included.

ideas.what: Definition and study of the double series Σ H_k^{(n)}/k^m (star double zeta values)
ideas.modern_name: Multiple (double) zeta values / Euler sums ζ*(m,n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (with Goldbach), correspondence 1742–43 and E477; modern revival by Hoffman, Zagier (1990s)

ideas.what: Announcement that the series reduce, via a product lemma, to products of zeta values (reflection formula)
ideas.modern_name: Stuffle / harmonic-product relation ζ(m)ζ(n) = ζ(m,n) + ζ(n,m) + ζ(m+n)

ideas.what: Attribution of most of the results to Goldbach
ideas.where_published: E477 preface; Opera omnia I.15 commentary

deep.surprise_reason: This is the famous founding paper of double zeta values. It and the Goldbach attribution are extensively discussed in the modern MZV literature (Hoffman, Zagier, Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst, Sandifer). This page is only a preface with the definition, so nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'coluerum' is how the scan appears, but the intended Latin is likely 'colueram' (or a printing variant). Uncertain.
